title: Passive-to-active switchover playbook with state consistency validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: produce a deterministic, testable passive->active switchover playbook for multi-region active-passive topology that validates state consistency (KV caches, tokenstore, user sessions), enforces SLO-aware traffic pacing, and runs an end-to-end backup/restore verification suite before and after the drill. This ticket captures the playbook, validation harness, and post-drill artifact links.

Rationale: previous drills focused on routing and service availability but surfaced latent state drift (KV cache divergence) and flaky restore checks in tokenstore. This playbook adds explicit resync and integrity checks plus automated smoke tests to reduce manual verification time and make drill outcomes repeatable.

Scope:
- Pre-drill gating and SLO verification (latency/error budgets, target saturation percentages).
- Controlled traffic pacing into passive region during switchover to avoid cache-stampede.
- Circuit-breaker tuning and load-shedding policy sample configs for the public API and internal batch endpoints.
- Backup snapshot integrity and restore validation: checksum, object counts, and functional query checks.
- Post-switchover consistency checks: KV cache diff, tokenstore replay, and end-to-end sample request traces validated against golden responses.
- Rollback criteria and automated rollback steps if state checks fail.

Non-goals: full DB cross-region replication (out of scope), long-running data rehydration post-drill (handed to Seq infra).

Runbook links and artifacts:
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DR/Passive-to-Active+Switchover+Playbook+v1.0
- Backup/restore harness repo (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/dr-restore-harness/pull/86
- Draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/DR/switchover-validation?orgId=1
- SLO page + alerting policy: https://observability.redwood.ai/slo/passive-region-slo
- Example GH run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dr-restore-harness/actions/runs/123456789

Key safety preconditions (must pass before proceeding):
1) Current error-rate SLOs for serving tier < 0.5% 5m window and sustained latency p95 < 250ms for 15m.
2) Backups in object storage newer than 30m and with successful checksum verification.
3) Circuit-breaker experiment established on a small production shadow route with configured trip thresholds (5xx > 1% for 5m or latency p95 > 500ms).
4) On-call + cross-functional DR runbook confirmations sent to #oncall-dr and #infra-ops 24h prior.

Top-level playbook steps (condensed):
- Pre-checks (T-2h): verify backups, run restore-harness sanity on a staging snapshot, ensure monitoring and pager rotations are configured.
- Warmup (T-1h): start passive region in cold-standby mode, run KV cache warmers with low-fanout traffic, ensure tokenstore read replicas catch up.
- Enforce traffic pacing (T0-T+10m): gradually ramp traffic to passive region at configurable increments (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) over 10 minutes; observe SLOs and circuit-breaker signals at each stage.
- State validation (T+10m): run KV cache diff job, tokenstore replay check, and golden-path smoke tests (user login, chat generation, embed lookup).
- Full acceptance: if all validations pass, mark passive region active in Console and update routing policy.
- Post-switchover backups: trigger a full snapshot and run restore-verify on the new active region.
- Rollback: if any validation fails, immediately throttle traffic back to previous region, enact circuit-breaker rule to block new sessions in passive region, and run post-failure analysis.

Validation harness specifics:
- KV diff tool compares keysets + value-hash counts and reports top-50 divergent keys with sample values.
- Tokenstore restore verification replays 1000 anonymized session tokens against the active store and verifies auth flows.
- Golden-path smoke tests execute example prompts and compare deterministic fields (status codes, schema keys) and fuzzy-match model outputs with tolerance.

Circuit breaker & load-shedding policy examples (stored in repo):
- public-api-cb.yaml: trip when 5xx > 0.8% over 2m OR p95 lat > 500ms for 3m; open for 2m half-open probing.
- batch-ingest-shed.yaml: shed lowest-priority jobs when CPU > 85% or queue latency > 2m.

Rollout and approval:
- Requires DR lead + SRE manager approval in the Confluence checklist before run.
- Post-drill review and write-up -> runtime-1.20 retrospective doc.

Expected deliverables:
- Completed playbook with automated validation scripts checked into dr-restore-harness repo.
- Grafana dashboard panels for immediate pass/fail indicators.
- A reproducible test rig in CI to run the restore verification in non-prod nightly.

Notes/assumptions:
- Some KV namespaces are eventual-consistency tolerant (marked in the runbook). The playbook contains namespace-specific rules to allow controlled divergence where acceptable.
- If model-serving cache warmers hit cold-start penalties, there is a fallback plan to spin up additional inference slots from Dedicated pool to avoid user-facing latency.

Next steps:
1) Finish the restore harness PR and get 2 approvers (PR: #86).
2) Wire dashboard panels and alert rules (owner: PagerDuty-DR).
3) Schedule drill with customer-impact simulation window and announce to stakeholders.

Contact: Marcus Nguyen (assignee) for operational questions, Aisha Patel (creator) for playbook content decisions.

runbook_steps: Pre-checks: verify SLOs, backups, and monitoring with the pre-flight script.
Warmup: start passive region services in warm mode and run cache warmers.
Pacing: ramp traffic in increments with SLO gating after each increment.
Validate: run KV diff, tokenstore replay, and golden-path smoke tests.
Commit: update routing policy and mark region active if validations pass.
Post-backup: trigger fresh snapshot and run restore-verify on the new active region.
Rollback: throttle traffic back and engage circuit-breaker rules if any validation fails.
Postmortem: collect logs, save artifacts, and publish remediation tasks.
